notes: Account background: mid-size capital markets / trading desk with high-frequency chat assistants and realtime reranking needs.
Primary ask: Guaranteed throughput during market hours (08:00-20:00 ET) + tight latency SLOs for customer-facing features.
Throughput targets: sustain 1,200 inference req/s during peak windows; burst to 3,000 req/s for <30m events.
Latency targets (customer): p95 < 60ms for short prompts; p99 <= 180ms measured at edge (observed in POC: p99 ~210ms, needs improvement).
Reserved GPU planning: customer prefers reserved footprint equivalent to 4x H100 (est. capacity) + 2-node hot-burst pool. Wants explicit reservation in SOW.
- Uptime target requested: 99.95% (customer asks for 99.97% during market hours) - see SLA draft.
- Credit schedule proposed by customer: 10% credit for monthly uptime 99.90-99.95%; 25% for 99.50-99.90%; 100% for <99.50% (Redwood initial counter smaller tiers).
- Maintenance windows: customer requests fixed monthly 2-4h windows outside 08:00-20:00 ET; advance notice >=72h and ability to opt-out for critical market days.
- Support SLAs: P1 response <= 1 hour, P2 <= 4 hours, P3 <= 24 hours. Customer expects dedicated escalation path (phone + Slack).
Key security asks: customer-managed KMS for model input storage; SOC2 + additional pen-test report; audit logs for all request/response metadata.
POC notes: ran A/B tests vs Anthropic hosted endpoints - Redwood dedicated showed 18% lower median latency under batching but higher tail; tuning batching config suggested.
Cost sensitivity: high. Wants predictable reserved commit with clear per-token burn vs burst pricing. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations to reduce token costs.
Quote from CTO call (2026-02-05): 'We can't tolerate unpredictability in tail latency on trade days. Maintenance cannot be a surprise.'
Open technical items: kernel selection for long-context models, KV cache warmup for burst windows, canary routing to fallback models when capacity constrained.
Legal/Procurement: procurement requested sample SLA language re: credits and force majeure exclusions; legal asked for examples from existing enterprise contracts.
